suite_baseline.reconciliation: As recorded in parity/control-plane.ledger.json: 2194 collected + 5 modules skipped at collection time = 2199. Unchanged by this belt.

subsystem.name: canary
subsystem.note: The item 10 routing rehearsal, interlock tests/canary, 6 files. One ledger per source file. Not to be confused with parity/measurement.canary.ledger.json, which ports tests/measurement/test_canary.py -- the measurement harness's view of a canary, not the canary's own store. The two names sit next to each other in parity/ and mean different things.

file.note: The inventory is `pytest --collect-only -q` on the source at 65f36c5, in collection order; all 8 pass there (measured 2026-08-28 against the shared read-only clone of interlock at 65f36c5, `PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q tests/canary/ -p no:cacheprovider`: 70 passed, of which 8 are tests/canary/test_synthetic_v1.py's).

systematic_mappings.to: exported canonicalJson() in src/canary/synthetic_v1.ts, plus a private canonicalJsonString() and a byCodePoint comparator
systematic_mappings.why: JSON.stringify neither sorts keys, nor omits the spaces json.dumps would default to, nor escapes non-ASCII. Written inside the canary package rather than reusing src/fencing/pyjson.ts's complete pyJsonDumps because the canary package imports no other runtime module (the structural belt asserts it). Verified byte-for-byte against CPython including a surrogate pair.
systematic_mappings.affects: every written line; audit.ts (LANE D) should import it

systematic_mappings.to: a private splitLines() scanner over the code-unit boundary set {LF, VT, FF, CR, FS, GS, RS, NEL, U+2028, U+2029} with CRLF as one boundary
systematic_mappings.why: `"".split("\n")` is `[""]` in JavaScript -- one bogus empty line that fails JSON.parse and turns a legitimately empty store into a refused one, which would break every other case in the belt. Written as a scan rather than a regex character class because biome's noControlCharactersInRegex (rightly) refuses \x1c-\x1e inside a literal. Behaviour compared against CPython on 8 shapes, all identical.
systematic_mappings.affects: records() line splitting and line numbering

systematic_mappings.from: json.JSONDecodeError's str() interpolated into the refusal message ('Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)')
systematic_mappings.to: String(error) on the JS SyntaxError ('SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input')
systematic_mappings.why: There is no cross-runtime parser-error text. The message SHAPE is identical (`<path>:<line> is not a record: <error>; a broken store is refused, not read as empty`); only the parser's own wording differs, and no ported assertion looks at it (the source's match is `refused|not a record`).

`existsSync` would accept a directory, and a plain `statSync` throws ENOENT instead of reaching the refusal. Python's is_file() answers false for both absent and non-file and follows symlinks; this does the same. (One residual gap: is_file() also swallows EACCES on a parent, which throwIfNoEntry:false does not.)

The exclusive-create flag is the property under test, not the refusal: an existsSync-then-write port passes the ported case and reintroduces the race the source's comment says it closes. Classified by errno code, never by message text.
TypeScript has no keyword-only parameters; the contract fixes this shape for the whole belt so call sites stay consistent. 1_700_000_000_000 < 2^53, so plain `number` -- no BigInt.
systematic_mappings.affects: startRun / finishRun signatures and every call site

systematic_mappings.to: a `newStore()` function called inside each test
systematic_mappings.why: Convention rule 8: function-scoped fixtures translate to a plain call, not beforeEach. The directory comes from caseRoot("cnry-syn") -- a short nickname per D-0020, because the directory name is interpolated into every refusal message these cases `match` against as a search.

D-0015: readFileSync(p, "utf-8") substitutes U+FFFD, which would turn damaged bytes into plausible-looking records instead of an error. Python raises UnicodeDecodeError; this raises a TypeError, and in both the error propagates unwrapped rather than becoming a refusal.

systematic_mappings.from: `"run_id" not in record` on a dict
systematic_mappings.to: Object.hasOwn(parsed, "run_id") with an explicit isRecord() guard
systematic_mappings.why: Rule 9. JS `in` walks the prototype chain, so a record could appear to carry `constructor`/`toString`; and `typeof x === "object"` is true for null and arrays, which `isinstance(record, dict)` excludes.

systematic_mappings.from: sorted() over str (code-point order), returning a tuple
systematic_mappings.why: JavaScript's default comparator sorts by UTF-16 code unit and disagrees with Python above the BMP. Immutability of the tuple maps to `readonly`, and the ported case compares with toEqual on an array so the ORDER stays part of the assertion.
D-0017: repr becomes hand-written quotes, never JSON.stringify.
Same chain-preserving semantics; `name` plus `Object.setPrototypeOf` in the constructor so `instanceof` (and therefore expectRefusal's type half) holds.

target_only_tests.why: None. Every collected test in this file is a translation of a source case.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The store is single-writer: startRun/finishRun are a read (records()) followed by an append, so two concurrent writers can interleave and both append a start for the same run.
inherited_limitations.why: The source says so explicitly and declines to fix it -- 'a stand-in that quietly did would be one more thing the rehearsal appeared to prove and had not'. Reproduced, and the module docstring carries the source's reasoning.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: startRun refuses any run id present in ANY record, so a store holding only a run_finished record for X refuses startRun(X) even though X was never started here.
inherited_limitations.why: The source's guard is `if run_id in self.run_ids()`, not against the started set. Narrowing it would be a different function; the message ('was already started') is wider than it sounds and is kept verbatim.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: A blank line in the MIDDLE of the store refuses the whole store (json.loads('') raises), and a store ending in two newlines is likewise refused.
inherited_limitations.why: Python's splitlines keeps interior empty lines and json.loads refuses them; reproduced deliberately, and confirmed identical to CPython on both shapes. NOTE: this contradicts CONTRACT.md, which says records() skips blank lines -- see concerns.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: #append reads the file to inspect the last byte, so appending to a store whose file has been deleted since construction raises ENOENT rather than a refusal.
inherited_limitations.why: Python's `self._path.read_bytes()[-1:]` raises FileNotFoundError the same way; only reachable by deleting the file between calls, and the source does not guard it.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: A record whose run_id is not a string (a number, null, an object) is rendered with String() into the id set instead of raising.
inherited_limitations.why: The source neither type-checks run_id nor could sort a mixed set -- Python's sorted() would raise TypeError there. Adding a refusal would be a guard the source does not have (rule 0 ceiling), so the wider behaviour is documented at the site (runIdOf) rather than fixed.

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > creation refuses an existing path
entries.reason: Straight translation. The source's unused `tmp_path` parameter is dropped (the `store` fixture already created the file); `pytest.raises(SyntheticStoreRefusal, match="already exists")` becomes `expectRefusal(..., SyntheticStoreRefusal, /already exists/)`.

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > a run starts once
entries.reason: Straight translation, including the second start's later timestamp (T0+1) that makes the refusal keyed on the id and not the clock. Asserts the substring, as the source does, not the whole message.

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > finishing appends rather than edits
entries.reason: Both halves kept: raw-text `after.startsWith(before)` read straight off the file, and the record-type order `["run_started", "run_finished"]` from `records()` in file order. `assert after.startswith(before)` maps to `expect(after.startsWith(before)).toBe(true)`.

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > a finish needs a start and happens once
entries.reason: All three properties in one case, in the source's order: 'never started' against a ZERO-BYTE store (so `records()` must read an empty file as no records rather than as one bogus line), then a start+finish, then 'already finished'. The two refusal substrings are distinct and both are asserted.

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > a broken store is refused, not read as empty
entries.reason: Both refusals kept, and the source's alternation `match="refused|not a record"` is kept as an alternation regex rather than narrowed to one wording (a narrowed pattern would assert more than the source). Fixture bytes are byte-identical to the source's (valid line 1, `not json` line 2). The absent store is CONSTRUCTED OUTSIDE the refusal assertion, which only a lazy constructor survives. Title punctuation: the source name has no comma; the prose sentence reads 'a broken store is refused, not read as empty' — the comma is in the target title, so use the id exactly as listed.

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > a record without a run_id is refused
entries.reason: Straight translation; same fixture line, same `match="run_id"`. The implementation checks key PRESENCE (`Object.hasOwn`), not truthiness, so `"run_id": null` or `""` is not refused by this branch — as in the source.

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > an append does not fuse onto a torn tail
entries.reason: Straight translation. `read_text().rstrip("\n")` maps to `.replace(/\n+$/u, "")` (strips every trailing newline, as rstrip does) and the rewrite is a truncating `writeFileSync`, not an append. Both assertions kept: `records()` has length 1 despite the torn tail, then the run ids in FILE order after the follow-on append (via `records()`, not `runIds()`).

entries.target_id: test/canary/synthetic-v1.test.ts::the stand-in counterparty's store > run ids answer the audit question
entries.reason: Straight translation. Python's tuple `("run-a", "run-b")` becomes `toEqual(["run-a", "run-b"])` on a `readonly string[]` — an ordered comparison, so the dedup AND the sort are both still asserted (the file order is run-b, run-a, run-b).
